title: Platform standup - 2026-04-03
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Miguel, Ravi, Sofia, Olivia (oncall)

Quick summary:
- Focus this week on control plane rollout (canary -> gradual), routing policy fixes, quota enforcement edge cases, and small auth bug in token refresh path.
- Oncall page: increased 500s from control-plane leader election during the EU region deployment yesterday; mitigated by fallback routing.

Control plane:
- MIG-342 (follow-up): Canary rollout for CP v2 started 2026-04-02 02:30 UTC. Initial metrics looked good but we saw GC spikes causing ~250ms request tails for admin endpoints.
- Action: Miguel to land small GC tuning PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/342) today; coordinate with release-engineering for restart window.
- Note: need to add a synthetic smoke test that exercises leader election latency under load (create ticket JIRA-PLAT-512).
- TODO: Add health-check to short-circuit non-critical admin queries during leader election (Ravi).

Routing:
- Observed route thrash when fallback rules triggered; root cause appears to be TTL on route cache being 30s which collides with burst traffic patterns.
- Temporary mitigation: reduce cache TTL to 10s (deployed to canary) while we profile.
- Longer term: implement adaptive TTL based on route stability metrics (outline in Confluence: Control Plane Design page).
- Blocker: Need test harness for multi-region failover to reproduce exact sequence that caused thrash. Sofia to pair with infra-testing next Tues.

Auth / token refresh:
- Reported: rare 401s during token refresh (edge case when refresh token rotated concurrently for the same session). Repro steps in linked Slack thread.
- Root cause suspicion: race in token rotation handler when refresh and revoke run simultaneously.
- Action items: add per-session refresh lock to prevent concurrent rotations (Ravi), add a non-blocking retry path for auth middleware to avoid 401s on transient errors.
- Linked PR template started: auth-refresh-lock WIP.

Quotas / rate limiting:
- Quota enforcement logs show mismatch between quota shard counters and central quota service after network partition. Counters drift ~0.5% under heavy churn.
- Short term: introduce reconciliation job to run every 5m to reconcile hot shards (Miguel).
- Long term: design idempotent counter updates or vector-clock style reconciliation. Raised JIRA-PLAT-498 to track.
- Observability: add quota-debug mode that dumps top-10 hot keys to logs for 15m window for debugging (Sofia).

Oncall notes / recent incidents:
- Incident #INC-2026-04-02-A: Region EU fallback triggered due to control-plane leader election taking 12s on one CF node. Impact: short increase in 500s for management endpoints, app traffic unaffected due to routing fallback. Post-mortem draft started in Confluence.
- Mitigation: tuned GC and added temporary fallback TTL reduction. Need formal runbook update.

Action items (owner / eta):
- Miguel: land GC tuning PR and reconciliation job prototype (ETA: 2026-04-04).
- Ravi: implement per-session refresh lock + unit tests (ETA: 2026-04-06).
- Sofia: infra test harness for multi-region failover + quota-debug mode (ETA: 2026-04-09).
- Aisha: coordinate canary restarts with release-eng and update runbook (ETA: 2026-04-05).

Follow-ups / discussion points for next week:
- Decide on adaptive TTL strategy for route cache (tradeoffs: consistency vs. tail latency).
- Quota model: explore bounded counters or CRDT approach; schedule architecture sync with applied-ml (sampling) and observability teams.
- Auth: confirm if token rotation frequency needs to change for high-churn customers.

Notes to self:
- Keep canary small until GC tuning fully validated.
- Add a dashboard panel for leader election duration (histogram) and correlate with admin 5xx spikes.

Links referenced in notes:
- Control Plane Design (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Control+Plane+Design
- Related Jira: JIRA-PLAT-512 (leader election test), JIRA-PLAT-498 (quota reconciliation)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/342
- Slack incident thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123ABCD/p1671234567890

End of notes.
